sections.h2: Who records a deed in Mohave County, Arizona?
sections.html:
The Mohave County Recorder records deeds, mortgages, liens, releases, affidavits and plats for the whole county. The main office is at 700 West Beale Street in Kingman, and the phone is (928) 753-0701.

Mohave County covers about 13,461 square miles in the northwest corner of Arizona, and the Recorder runs three counter locations so a seller in Bullhead City or Lake Havasu City does not have to drive to the county seat. Mail goes to P.O. Box 7000, Kingman, AZ 86402. The office is closed on observed holidays.

  • Kingman (main office): 700 West Beale Street, (928) 753-0701, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Bullhead City: 1130 Hancock Rd, (928) 758-0701 ext. 2026, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Thursday, closed noon to 1 p.m.
  • Lake Havasu City: 2001 College Dr, Ste 93, (928) 453-0702 ext. 3021, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed noon to 1 p.m.

The Recorder staff will not tell you how to word a deed or whose name belongs on it. Their FAQ says those questions are legal advice and sends you to an attorney, a title company or a paralegal.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Mohave County?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $30.00 to record in Mohave County. That flat fee applies to all documents unless the fee schedule names a different amount, and it has been in effect since July 1, 2019 under A.R.S. 11-475.

The fee does not change with the sale price. A $90,000 cabin in Golden Valley and a $450,000 house in Lake Havasu City pay the same recording fee, though the Affidavit of Property Value that rides with the deed asks for the price. Make checks payable to the Mohave County Recorder.

ItemMohave County fee
Recording, all documents unless otherwise specified$30.00
Instruments from governmental agencies$15.00
Copies of records, per page$1.00
Certification, per document$3.00
Conformed copy, each$1.50
Military dischargesNo charge (A.R.S. 11-465)
Subdivision plat, first page / each added page$24.00 / $20.00

Source: Mohave County Recorder, Recording Fees. Credit cards are accepted at the counter and on the self-service site, with a transaction charge added.

sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax when you sell a house in Mohave County?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee schedule lists no tax or fee that scales with the sale price. Arizona's constitution, Article 9, Section 24, bars the state, counties and cities from imposing any new tax, fee or stamp requirement on selling or conveying real property. The only carve-out covers charges that already existed on December 31, 2007.

What the county does require is paperwork. Under A.R.S. 11-1133, each deed that transfers title must carry an Affidavit of Property Value signed by the buyer and the seller or their agents. It lists names, mailing addresses, the legal description, the situs address, the sale date, the total consideration, the way the deal was financed and the assessor's parcel number. If the affidavit is incomplete, the recorder must refuse the deed unless it bears a valid exemption notation.

Mohave County's FAQ says every sale needs a fully completed affidavit or an exemption number printed on the document, and the exemption list sits on page two of the form.

sections.h2: Which Mohave County transfers skip the Affidavit of Property Value?
sections.html:
A.R.S. 11-1134 lists the exempt transfers, and the deed has to note the specific exemption claimed on its face. Several of them matter to families handling an estate or a divorce.

  • A deed of gift, and a quitclaim deed executed for no monetary consideration.
  • A conveyance made under a court order.
  • A transfer with only nominal consideration for residential property between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, or siblings.
  • A trustee's deed under a deed of trust power of sale, and a transfer made to provide or release security for a debt.
  • A transfer from a person to a trustee, or from a trustee to a trust beneficiary, for nominal consideration.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded.

A sale to a cash buyer does not fall in any of these categories, so a normal sale needs the full affidavit. When you are unsure whether an exemption applies, ask the title company that is closing the deal before the deed reaches the counter.

sections.h2: How do you present a deed for recording in Mohave County?
sections.html:
Bring the original signed and notarized deed to any of the three offices, or mail it to P.O. Box 7000, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the fee enclosed. The office checks it against the requirements of A.R.S. 11-480, assigns a recording number and makes it permanent record.

Walk-in documents are scanned and handed back the same visit. Mailed originals are scanned and then returned to the return address on the document, which the office says takes roughly 4 to 6 weeks. Indexers then enter the parties and parcel so the deed can be found later.

One warning on the FAQ page is worth repeating: once a document is recorded it cannot be removed under any circumstances. A wrong legal description or a misspelled name means a second corrective document and a second fee. Read the deed twice before it goes in.

sections.h2: How can you check liens and get copies of a deed in Mohave County?
sections.html:
The Recorder runs a free Recorded Document Search on its self-service site. The Recorder suggests searching by name in the both-name fields, last name first.

Copies of a recorded deed are $1.00 per page in person, by mail, online or by phone at (928) 753-0701. You need the book and page, the fee number, the recording date or the names on the document. If you ask by mail, include a self-addressed stamped envelope.

The office says its search does not guarantee that a property is free of liens, and it will help you learn the search but will not research for you. Title insurance from a title company is the proper protection. If you are selling a house with unpaid tax, a judgment or a lien on it, a title search before listing shows what has to be cleared at closing.

sections.h2: How big is Mohave County and what does the housing stock look like?
sections.html:
Mohave County is the second-largest county in Arizona by area at 13,461 square miles, and it is split into two sections by the Grand Canyon. The larger and more populated southern section runs along the Colorado River and includes Kingman, Bullhead City, Lake Havasu City and part of the Mojave Desert.

The 2020 census counted 213,267 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 228,102. That census also counted 117,650 housing units, with 22.4% vacant, and of the occupied homes 71.7% were owner-occupied. Lake Havasu City is the largest city, Kingman has been the county seat since 1887.

School districts include Kingman Unified, Lake Havasu Unified and Bullhead City Elementary. For zoning, permits and septic questions on a rural parcel outside the cities, the county's Development Services office at (928) 757-0903 handles the unincorporated areas.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax after the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Recorder sends recorded documents to the Assessor, who updates ownership on the tax roll. The Assessor's office says more than 200 recorded documents arrive from the Recorder every day, so ownership changes enter a steady queue.

The Treasurer's FAQ says the only way to change the owner name on real property is to record a legal document with the Recorder. If the seller still gets a tax bill after closing, the Treasurer asks that it be forwarded to the new owner or mailed back to P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with a note that the property was sold. For tax amounts, due dates and appeals, see the Mohave County property tax guide.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Mohave County, AZ?
faqs.a: It costs $30.00 per document, the standard fee under A.R.S. 11-475 since July 1, 2019. Government agency instruments are $15.00, copies are $1.00 per page and certification is $3.00 per document. Checks go to the Mohave County Recorder.

faqs.q: Does Mohave County charge a real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Recorder's fee schedule lists none. Arizona's Constitution, Article 9, Section 24, bars new taxes or fees on selling or conveying real property, apart from charges that existed on December 31, 2007. You still file an Affidavit of Property Value with the deed.

faqs.q: Where is the Mohave County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: The main office is at 700 West Beale Street, Kingman, AZ 86401, phone (928) 753-0701, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. There are also offices at 1130 Hancock Rd in Bullhead City and 2001 College Dr, Ste 93 in Lake Havasu City, both closed from noon to 1 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Mohave County Recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Mail the original to P.O. Box 7000, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the correct fee. The office scans it and returns the original to the return address, which it says takes about 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: Can the Mohave County Recorder tell me whose name belongs on my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office treats questions about adding, removing or changing owners as legal advice and refers people to an attorney, title company or paralegal. It will explain how to search records and how to submit a document.
